memory_leads.lead: Distress communications involve distinct roles rather than one ship-to-shore call: onboard command/bridge or radio functions, company/shore contacts, coast-station or rescue-coordination functions, satellite or terrestrial communication services, nearby vessels and dedicated search-and-rescue assets can each receive, relay or act on different information.

Communications readiness is a pre-event operational state: installed systems, power/backup availability, antenna or terminal operability, configured identity/location information, routine test/maintenance state and crew familiarity can diverge without establishing compliance or prescribing how to operate equipment.

A distress alert has separate origination, transmission, reception and acknowledgement states. The time an onboard party initiates an alert is not automatically the time a shore authority or assisting vessel receives, understands or accepts responsibility for coordination.

Alert relay and validation are their own states. An alert may be repeated or relayed through different paths, updated with better position/situation information, or investigated as uncertain/false without blind Memory asserting any specific signaling procedure or event outcome.

Rescue coordination should be represented as case activation, information gathering, geographic/operational responsibility determination, tasking or requesting assistance, ongoing coordination and later stand-down/closure rather than as a single 'SAR launched' timestamp.

Position, identity and casualty-condition information can improve or degrade through the event. Initial reported location, automatically supplied information, later bridge/crew updates and independently observed positions should remain distinct known-time observations rather than being overwritten by a final reconstructed position.

On-scene communications are a separate coordination layer after search/rescue resources or nearby vessels become involved. Participants can have different information, communications reach and task status; exact command arrangements and search tactics remain source- and event-specific.

Nearby commercial vessels are potential assistance capacity, not automatically assigned rescue assets. Their receipt of information, feasibility of diversion, response/coordination state and actual arrival/assistance can differ and can affect voyage disruption without proving a legal duty in any specific case.

Dedicated rescue assets have their own availability chain: alerting/tasking, crew/asset readiness, departure, transit, on-scene arrival, assistance/recovery and return-to-service. Nominal regional SAR capability is therefore not equivalent to immediate assistance at a given historical moment.

Distress-related locating and survival-communications devices should be treated as a family of independent readiness/activation/detection states rather than one 'beacon worked' flag. Exact carriage rules, frequencies, activation methods and performance require authoritative Evidence.

Communications degradation can trigger redundancy changes and information-quality loss: one path may fail, coverage may vary or backup arrangements may become relevant. The structural state is useful for replay, but blind Memory must not give troubleshooting instructions or infer why a system failed.

Rescue does not end at first contact. Survivor recovery, medical/shore handoff, accounting for persons, vessel abandonment/recovery interface, company/authority notification and later repatriation or care can have separate completion times.

Distress/SAR records have their own known-time trail: transmitted/received alerts, coordination logs, position updates, asset-tasking records and later reports may not align perfectly. Later consolidated incident narratives must not be backfilled into the information available to participants during the event.

P061 navigation memory is refined because the bridge's last known navigation/position/information state becomes an input to distress communications, but later SAR position reconstruction must not overwrite what the bridge or shore side actually knew when the alert was first sent or received.

P054 casualty memory is refined because emergency response has an information-and-coordination backbone: casualty stabilization, towing/salvage and place-of-refuge decisions may depend on when distress information reaches authorities and helpers, while communications state does not itself establish casualty cause.

P057 technical-management memory is refined because communications and locating equipment can have maintenance/test/defect states whose operational consequence appears only if degraded readiness intersects with an actual emergency; an open defect is not proof that an alert failed.

P059/P060 crewing and SMS memory are refined because drill/familiarization and actual emergency performance are distinct: training completion can affect readiness but cannot be used to infer how an individual or crew acted in a real distress event.

P054 already covers physical casualty response, salvage, emergency tow and investigation. P062 adds the distress-information and SAR-coordination state rather than duplicating physical recovery mechanics.

P060 already covers emergency drills and incident-response process inside the SMS. P062 reuses that preparation boundary but focuses on the real-time external communications/rescue network, not another onboard procedure catalog.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Operational distress instructions are safety-critical and require authoritative current rules/training, not blind Memory.
Equipment/regulatory requirements vary by vessel, sea area, flag and rule vintage and require Evidence.
Event-specific operational/legal conclusions require authoritative records and are outside a blind structural pass.
Provider/authority identity and current capability are source-first questions outside blind Memory.

stop_reason: The distress/SAR layer is populated from communications readiness through alert origination/reception/acknowledgement, relay/update, rescue coordination, nearby/dedicated assistance, locating/survival-device state, degraded communications, recovery/handoff and records. Further recall becomes equipment-, frequency-, procedure-, search-pattern-, provider-, event- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation and not distress, radio, GMDSS, search-and-rescue, navigation, safety, medical, regulatory, operational or legal advice; no frequency, channel, procedure, equipment requirement, alert status, location, search pattern, rescue tactic, legal duty, incident fault, provider capability or jurisdictional conclusion is verified.
